outcome: Tenascin C levels in breast milk
Granzyme B levels in breast milk
cohort: The study included 60 breastfeeding mothers: 50 who were either vaccinated against SARS-CoV-2 or had recovered from infection, and a control group of 10 unvaccinated mothers with no history of COVID-19.
finding: All targeted antimicrobial and immune-regulatory biomarkers were detected in breast milk, providing insights into the immune profile transferred to infants and reinforcing breastfeeding's role in anti-SARS-CoV-2 defense.
mod_finding: Breast milk protein levels were found to be influenced by delivery mode.
cross-section timing: During lactation, with samples collected from breastfeeding mothers at varying infant ages.
